Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Longitudinal ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN after transient stimulus ("unmask" latent enhancers)
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., macrophages, fibroblasts) with a transient signal, then profile chromatin accessibility and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) binding at timepoints through weeks after washout. Memory is supported if AP-1-bound enhancers stay open and primed after stimulus clearance, analogous to 'unmasking' hidden regions, and give faster, stronger transcription upon restimulation.

ideas.title: Acute degron depletion of AP-1 during vs after priming
ideas.description: Use dTAG/auxin degrons on JUN/FOS or dominant-negative A-FOS, depleting AP-1 either only during priming or only after priming (maintenance phase). If priming-phase loss abolishes the enhanced secondary response while maintenance-phase loss does not, AP-1 is needed for establishment but not for maintenance. The reverse pattern would show AP-1 itself maintains the memory.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage/history tracing of AP-1 activity
ideas.description: Combine an AP-1 reporter or recorder (e.g., Cre-based or fluorescent timer under TRE elements) with scRNA/ATAC multiome to label cells that experienced AP-1 activity and follow them after rest. Test whether past AP-1 history predicts accessibility state and restimulation response in individual cells, separating cell-autonomous memory from population heterogeneity.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 recruitment sufficiency test
ideas.description: Use a dCas9-based or optogenetic system to transiently recruit AP-1 factors (or their pioneer-like partners) to a defined locus with a reporter. Then remove the trigger and measure whether accessibility, histone marks (H3K27ac/H3K4me1) and responsiveness persist across cell divisions. Persistence sufficient to alter later induction would show AP-1 can initiate memory by itself.

ideas.title: Live-cell imaging and kinetic modeling of AP-1 dynamics and division inheritance
ideas.description: Track endogenously tagged FOS/JUN with single-molecule or live imaging, and measure binding residence time, nuclear levels, and mitotic bookmarking across divisions in mother-daughter pairs. Fit mathematical models (bistable feedback vs. chromatin-based epigenetic memory) to see which explains retention and inheritance of responsiveness; AP-1 autoregulation (JUN induces JUN) is a natural positive-feedback candidate.
